requirement.title: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true
requirement.text:
#### Bug description

The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true. This has happened since version 3.1.1. It still worked in 3.1.0.

story: The change makes TypeCollector skip duplicate or mixed-kind keys instead of throwing, documents how the analyzer treats suppressed types, and adds analyzer and run-time tests for SuppressSourceGeneration types.

decisions.title: Dependency change in Directory.Packages.props
decisions.oneliner: Dependency and toolchain versions decide which users can build and run the package.
decisions.question: Accept this dependency or toolchain change?
decisions.routed_by: policy rule 'dependency': the reviewer may not decide this

decisions.title: No visible change to the suppress-skip path
decisions.oneliner: The diff never touches how the analyzer filters SuppressSourceGeneration types. It only guards Dictionary.Add, which also affects generated types. The link to the regression is unproven.
decisions.requirement_part: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true
decisions.would_be_wrong_if: The 3.1.1 regression was really an analyzer crash on duplicate keys, and the analyzer already visits suppressed types elsewhere.
decisions.question: Has anyone confirmed the new analyzer tests fail on the unpatched 3.1.1 code, for example MemberWithoutKeyIsReported?

decisions.title: Mixed-key member dropped, skipping later checks
decisions.oneliner: The new continue stops the member's type and formatter checks, so a MsgPack003 or formatter diagnostic on that member is now hidden. This also affects generated types.
quote: continue; // The key kind does not match the other members; the diagnostic is reported, so skip this member.
decisions.would_be_wrong_if: Code after the Add does not report diagnostics for the member, or hiding them behind MsgPack005 is acceptable.
decisions.question: Is it acceptable to hide other diagnostics on a member that has a mismatched key kind?

handled.title: Duplicate key silently keeps first member
handled.oneliner: The second member with the same key is now dropped without notice. The MsgPack005 report must come from somewhere else, which this diff does not show.
handled.would_be_wrong_if: A separate pass already reports duplicate keys before this point. The tests suggest so, but this is unverified.
handled.routed_by: low impact or no decision needed

handled.title: Run-time round-trip test does not cover the bug
handled.oneliner: This tests dynamic serialization and that no formatter is generated, but the bug is about analyzer diagnostics. It says nothing about the regression.
handled.would_be_wrong_if: The run-time resolver was also broken for suppressed types in 3.1.1.
handled.routed_by: low impact or no decision needed

handled.title: README section adds policy claims not requested
handled.oneliner: The new docs promise which diagnostics apply or are exempt, including MsgPack011, 016 and 017. The bug report did not ask for that, and it is a public commitment.
quote: The analyzer does not report the partial-class requirement ([MsgPack011](doc/analyzers/MsgPack011.md)) or the AOT-only checks ([MsgPack016](doc/analyzers/MsgPack016.md) and [MsgPack017](doc/analyzers/MsgPack017.md)) for these types, because they only apply when a formatter is generated.
handled.would_be_wrong_if: The maintainers already documented this behaviour as intended for suppressed types.
handled.question: Do you want this README section in a bug-fix change?
handled.routed_by: low impact or no decision needed

not_checked: The test suite was not run (no .NET SDK on the review host).
